response.answer: Top trends include advanced remote sensing for ecosystem valuation, scenario analysis using AI, and stakeholder engagement through digital platforms. Emerging technologies like quantum computing and AI drive digital transformation. Ecosystem thinking integrates business, innovation, and platform dynamics.

results.title: Streams and Sessions - iEMSs 2026
results.content: Sessions will highlight recent innovations in modelling (including applications), GHG accounting, soil carbon inventories and other foot printing methods, land-use change analysis, investigation and/or design of circularity in agricultural systems, scenario development, and model-data integration. The session welcomes applications related with, but not limited to water, air quality  and natural resources management to ecological footprint and circular economy or environmental policies, and works addressing issues related to data quality, explainability of models, and role in decision support processes. This includes, but is not limited to: Models for legacy and emerging contaminants; Integration of exposure models with models from other related fields, to better predict impacts; The use of models to inform policy decisions, mitigation measures and treaty negotiations; Data-driven, machine-learning and AI approaches for leveraging the increased availability of complex environmental data, and; Best practices in sharing, documenting and making FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reproducible) open-source software and data. This session explores how environmental modelling and integrated data systems can support sustainable development, habitat restoration and focused research by linking scientific insight, ecosystem dynamics, and stakeholder perspectives.
